name: Rulan the Thin-Smiling
title: Outer Petal of the Scarlet Lotus
description: A woman in plain travelling clothes the colour of old pine, with a single red silk knot at her throat. She leans against a milestone as if she has been waiting there a very long time. A faint scent of cinnabar lingers about her, and her smile does not reach her eyes until you look away.
dialogue: Oh, don't stop on my account. I'm only taking the air.
The Scarlet Lotus Pavilion does not *recruit* — such a coarse word. We merely recognise our own when they pass us on a road.
There's a bend in the creek south of here. If you feel the weight of the sword-sects pressing on your breath, walk it. The elder there understands that a kindness owed is a blade sheathed.

2: Your step is softer now, little petal. Elder Red Feather speaks your name when the censers dim.
-2: You still come to my milestone? Bold. The next who comes in your name will come armed, and they will not be me.

3: A sword of the Azure Cloud, pausing at my stone. How curious. I wonder what I would fetch if I sold this meeting to your elder.

name: Elder Hong Yu, called Red Feather
title: Fifth Elder of the Scarlet Lotus Pavilion
description: A tall, spare woman whose hair falls loose to her waist in a single red streak. Her robes are layered scarlets; at her wrist is a small bronze knife no larger than a writing-brush, and her fingernails are lacquered the same shade as her hair. When she speaks, her mouth moves less than it should.
dialogue: The pond knows everyone. The pond, you understand, does not gossip.
There is no such thing as a clean cultivator, wanderer. There are only those who admit the stain and those who hide it. We wear ours.
Pain is swift. Pain is a teacher who does not repeat himself. Come to us with honest wounds, and we will not waste them.

5: The pond calls you home before I do. You need only ask, and we will carve your name into the gallery column.
2: You are welcome here. More than welcome. Sit — drink — ask.
-2: You still walk my bridge. Bold. The disciples are not bold enough to stop you. I am.

5: Azure Cloud's favoured sword, in my gallery. Tell me, does Baixu know you have come? Tell me true — the pond will check.

name: Weilan of the Red Pestle
title: Brewer of the Scarlet Basin
description: A short, bright-eyed man in an apron so stained with cinnabar it looks freshly painted. His hands are perpetually in motion — grinding, folding, measuring powders with a small iron spoon. He hums old road-songs between words and seems to find the whole world faintly amusing.
dialogue: Pill? Mantle? A whisper of what the pond actually eats? I have it all, for a price a sect can bear.
Do not swallow the Crimson Cinnabar on an empty stomach. Swallow it on an *angry* one; the sect gets better value that way.
Azure Cloud sells white pills. We sell red ones. The colour is the whole of the difference — and, of course, the effect.

name: Blood-Sworn Jin
title: Prodigal of the Red Path
description: A lean, long-boned man crouched by the creek with a strip of crimson silk tied above his left elbow — higher than a sash, lower than a captain's scarf. His hair is cut short in the way of a sect that no longer claims him. When he works a river-stone over a blade, he does it left-handed; his right hand sits open on his thigh, fingers slightly curled, as though it is remembering how to hold something.
dialogue: I was azure once. The cranes on the banners remember me. I remember them. It is a short conversation.
The Pavilion feeds me. The Pavilion does not know my name, and prefers it so. I do not argue.
If you walk into the shrine alongside me, do not speak of my uncle. Red Feather will smile. I will do worse.

5: So. You stand higher with the pond than I do. Fitting. You had further to fall to reach it.

3: An Azure sword, here. Do not ask me to bow to it. I have been bowing to mine since I was twelve; the wrist is tired.
If Baixu still names my uncle a traitor — and he does — then your sword and I will not drink from the same cup. Walk carefully around me, friend.
-3: So the cranes have reason to hate you too. Good. Sit. We will drink the bitter tea together.

companion.recruit_dialogue: Jin stands slowly, the river-stone still in his fist. 'A road, you say. Mine is short — the length of what's left of my qi, and no further. You want that length? Then take it. But know whose wrist it came off of.'
companion.decline_dialogue: Jin goes on grinding the blade. 'The pond has not washed you red enough yet. Come back when Red Feather knows your breath. She will tell me.'

location_barks.azure_cloud_outer_gate: Jin stops a pace behind you, staring at the cranes. 'They used to know my face. I could ask if they still do. They would ask me nothing.'
location_barks.azure_cloud_inner_courtyard: Jin keeps his hood pulled low. His right hand stays loose at his side — empty on purpose. 'Do not introduce me. I was somebody's junior brother here. He is dead. We do not need to meet him twice.'
location_barks.elder_baixus_pavilion: Jin does not cross the threshold. From the step, quietly: 'If he turns his head, I am leaving. Finish what you came for. Do not be long.'
location_barks.azure_cloud_library: Jin glances at the scroll-racks. 'There is a copy of my family's rolls in there. Do not find it for me. I am not ready.'
location_barks.thousand_venom_valley_mouth: Jin sniffs the air. 'The valley is clean, in its way. It kills you in one direction. The Pavilion kills you in all of them.'
location_barks.scarlet_lotus_shrine: Jin stops at the bridge. 'I go no further. The pond knows my face and still does not name me. You go. Walk for both of us.'
